title: POC Weekly Sync - Quality Eval & Regression Check
summary: Weekly POC check-in to review latest quality evals on the pilot prompt set. SE reviewed scorecard changes showing slight regression on a subset of intents after the safety guardrail was tightened. Action items: run expanded eval with new scoring thresholds, provide per-intent breakdown, adjust prompts for problematic intents, share updated benchmark spreadsheet and security docs. Next call to validate updated numbers and decide on canary rollout for dedicated instances.
action_items: Samir Patel: Run expanded eval with updated prompt set (include hallucination / factuality metric and per-intent breakdown) (due 2025-10-24)
Alex Chen: Share updated benchmark spreadsheet + link to prompt set v3 and security checklist (due 2025-10-22)
Jordan Lee: Provide 200 additional priority prompts (edge-cases) to add to scoring harness (due 2025-10-23)
Marta Ruiz: Confirm SSO/SAML and KMS requirements for pilot environment and share any compliance docs (due 2025-10-27)
Priya Kapoor: Review proposed pass/fail thresholds and confirm success criteria for go/no-go (due 2025-10-28)
next_steps: Redwood SE to rerun eval with new scoring thresholds and include hallucination metric
AE to send updated pricing and proposed pilot timeline for dedicated capacity canary
Customer to upload additional prompt set examples and edge-case cases into shared sheet
Schedule next POC weekly sync for 2025-10-28 to review revised numbers
transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-10-21 15:00 UTC | Duration: ~45 mins | Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Samir (Redwood SE), Jordan (Acme ML), Priya (Acme PM), Marta (Acme SecOps)

00:00 Alex: okay everyone, thanks for joining the weekly POC sync, hope you're all good — quick agenda, run through the latest quality evals, look at regressions after we tightened the guardrails, and agree next steps. Samir, you wanna start with the numbers?
00:18 Samir: yeah sure, uh, thanks Alex. so the main change this week was we pushed prompt set v3 which includes the stricter safety filter — so we added a post-process filter and tightened the hallucination detector threshold. overall aggregate accuracy is stable at about 87%, down from 88% last week, but there's a regression on two intents: 'account-recon' and 'legal-summary'.
00:40 Jordan: right, we noticed that in our dashboard, for account-recon the precision dropped more than we'd expect. can you show per-intent numbers?
00:48 Samir: yep i have the per-intent breakdown in the sheet — i will share the link after, but quick callouts: account-recon F1 fell from 0.82 to 0.74, legal-summary F1 from 0.79 to 0.71. the other intents are roughly flat.
01:05 Priya: interesting, do you think that's because the guardrail is overzealous and the model is being too conservative? we're seeing overly short replies on legal-summary.
01:15 Samir: that's my theory. tightening hallucination cutoff reduced unsafe outputs but also clipped longer, context-rich responses. we could either relax the filter a bit or tweak the prompts to emphasize 'be thorough but factual'.
01:28 Marta: i want to flag sec requirements — if we relax filters that allow expanded outputs, we need to make sure our DLP and logging show no PII leakage. we need audit logs.
01:38 Alex: yep noted — Redwood can enable token-level tracing for the pilot (redwood console) and we can keep logs in customer-controlled KMS if you want. also we have a config to send audit logs to your SIEM.
01:54 Jordan: do we have numbers on hallucination rate when we loosen? like expected tradeoff?
02:00 Samir: not yet — that's the action item. i'll rerun the eval with a graduated set of thresholds (0.7, 0.8, 0.85) and include hallucination/ factuality metric as a separate column. we'll include per-intent baselines and delta.
02:18 Priya: and can you include latency and token cost impact? some of our cost modeling assumes average token length grows.
02:25 Samir: yes i'll add latency and estimated token cost per 1k requests. note that most of the cost increase is from response length and not from model changes; with Redwood Optimize we suggested batching for background workflows and prefix caching for repeated contexts.
02:43 Alex: quick question for Acme: are you leaning hosted or dedicated for the pilot? last time you said you'd consider dedicated if latency and QPS constraints hit a threshold.
02:52 Jordan: we want dedicated ideally but we need to confirm perf. our SLAs around 95th p latency at 350ms. is that feasible with the current model and your runtime?
03:02 Samir: for the model variant we're using, on dedicated gpus we've measured median ~120ms and 95th ~320ms when batched correctly. the NVMe-backed KV cache helps with repeated contexts, but it's sensitive to sequence length. we'll run a focused perf test on dedicated nodes as a canary.
03:20 Marta: and security-wise, dedicated needs VPC peering and our KMS integration. we need a list of certs and SOC2 scope.
03:28 Alex: we'll attach the security pack. i'll include SOC2 and the SSO/KMS integration notes in the doc i share.
03:36 Jordan: back to quality — on the legal-summary regression, can you show an example output? the one in the sheet looked like it cut off mid-sentence.
03:45 Samir: yeah here's an example, from the logs: 'Legal summary: The document establishes...' and then it truncates and adds a generic caveat. i think the guardrail triggered at the sentence boundary and invoked a fallback.
03:58 Priya: could that be a fallback policy misconfiguration? like we have automatic fallback to short safe responses when confidence low.
04:06 Samir: possible — i'll check routing policies and the fallback thresholds. sometimes the runtime swaps to a smaller safe model variant which returns conservative outputs; that explains short replies.
04:18 Jordan: okay so action plan is: rerun evals with graduated thresholds, include hallucination metric, provide per-intent breakdown, tweak prompts for legal-summary and account-recon, and check fallback policy.
04:30 Alex: perfect. i'll send pricing and canary plan for a dedicated capacity window for you to run perf tests. also we'll add SE-run perf benchmark + scripts so you can reproduce locally.
04:42 Priya: also, can you provide the prompt versions as separate files? we want to diff them.
04:47 Samir: yep will commit prompt_v2 / prompt_v3 in the shared drive and share link in the sheet.
04:52 Marta: last sec question, about audit logs retention — we need 7 years for this line of business. can Redwood support long-term retention?
05:00 Alex: yes we have add-on for extended observability retention. i'll include costs in the pricing doc.
05:07 Jordan: great. anything else from Redwood?
05:10 Samir: one small note — we noticed a small mismatch between tokenizer handling in our on-prem test harness and Redwood runtime: some special characters are tokenized differently which marginally changes scoring. not a big issue but worth aligning.
05:24 Jordan: thanks, we'll check our preprocessor.
05:26 Priya: ok wrap up — recap please Alex.
05:29 Alex: quick recap: Samir to rerun eval with updated thresholds + hallucination metric (due 10/24), Alex to share benchmark sheet, prompt v3 link, pricing and security pack (due 10/22), Acme to provide extra edge-case prompts and SSO/KMS details (due 10/23-10/27). next sync 2025-10-28. any objections?
05:50 Jordan: none here. thanks everyone.
05:52 Alex: thanks all, meeting adjourned.

Notes: transcript contains typical ASR imperfections: 'K V cash' spelled out in earlier auto-notes, occasional speaker mislabels in raw export.
